public_rationale: On April 29, 2026, Microsoft disclosed an AI annual revenue run rate above $37 billion for its fiscal third quarter; this was not realized annual revenue [e1]. Yahoo Finance reported combined 2026 capex guidance near $725 billion that day, but the packet does not reconcile that estimate with the claim's financial basis [e2]. Amazon's April 9 letter cited customer commitments in explaining its investment plans [e3]. These records establish neither the asserted sole cause of AI's economic presence nor the companies' complete motives [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: Comparable 2026 guidance and a complete set of 2027 plans available by July 7, 2026, are missing.
The packet does not provide a complete inventory of realized AI revenue disclosures across all four companies.
Run rates do not establish realized annual revenue or profitability, and management statements do not independently establish motives.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The only reason AI has any presence in the economy is that Microsoft, Google, Meta and Amazon intend to spend more than $765 billion in capex in 2026 and a trillion more in 2027 because they have no other hypergrowth ideas, even though generative AI has yet to show any real potential to drive meaningful revenues (let alone profits), as shown by none of them breaking out their AI revenues.

statement.excerpt: the only reason that AI has any presence in our economy is that Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Amazon are intent on spending more than $765 billion in capital expenditures in 2026 and a trillion more in 2027 because they have no other hypergrowth ideas, even though generative AI has yet to show any real potential as something that can drive meaningful revenues (let alone profits)

from_speaker: more than $765 billion in capital expenditures in 2026
because they have no other hypergrowth ideas
none of these companies break out their actual AI revenues
our_interpretation: The claim combines a sole-cause explanation, an assertion about corporate motives, spending intentions, and a revenue-disclosure premise. Verifying spending alone cannot establish the causal explanation.
The spending amounts describe plans known at publication, not a forecast of realized expenditure that should be graded after 2027.
The ordinary reading of actual revenues is realized revenue. An annualised revenue run rate is relevant context but is not interchangeable with realized annual revenue.
Meaningful revenues and hypergrowth have no stated thresholds. I do not supply numerical thresholds.
The financial scope below records the combined capex assertion. The text does not identify its accounting basis or explain how leases are treated.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence must establish the stated spending intentions on a comparable basis and show that those intentions, motivated by the absence of other growth opportunities, exclusively explain AI's economic presence. The revenue-disclosure premise also requires a review of disclosures available by publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence must establish an independent material cause of AI's economic presence, directly refute the asserted motives, or refute a factual premise using the same financial measure and period. A run-rate disclosure alone does not refute the narrower assertion about actual revenue.

evidence.excerpt: Our AI business surpassed $37 billion ARR, up 123%.
evidence.explanation: Microsoft disclosed a separate AI revenue run rate before the post. This challenges a broad reading of no AI revenue disclosure, but does not establish realized annual AI revenue, profits, or an independent cause of economic presence.

evidence.excerpt: that number is closer to $725 billion.
evidence.locator: Opening discussion of combined hyperscaler capital expenditure estimates
evidence.explanation: This contemporaneous comparison reports a combined high-end figure below Zitron's $765 billion. It is not decisive because a complete reconciliation of accounting conventions and any subsequent pre-post revisions was not established.

evidence.excerpt: We have customer commitments that make our capex investments predictable.
evidence.explanation: Amazon attributes its investment decisions partly to customer commitments. This supplies an alternative stated rationale, but management's account does not establish either the complete motive or the absence of other motives.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable 2026 and 2027 spending guidance available by July 7, 2026, a complete review of revenue disclosures available then, and independent evidence establishing the claimed exclusive cause or a material alternative cause of AI's economic presence.
